angada.text: Second `downsize` definition replaces the preceding five-argument definition in Ruby, so existing callers using `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now raise `ArgumentError` instead of downsizing. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, causing every emoji resize job to fail.

Client-side size check in `validateUploadedFile` is hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type instead of using the per-type site setting, allowing attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` to pass client validation

API image download cap is fixed at 10 MB which truncates downloads before the downsize loop can process them, breaking images larger than 10 MB and installations with `max_image_size_kb` configured above 10 MB

Downsize loop ignores failures and passes a percentage string to gifsicle for animated GIFs, but gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects WxH format, causing all five attempts to fail and the upload to fail with a misleading too-large error

Migration dereferences first result before fallback can run - if embed_category is absent, blank, or refers to deleted category, query returns no rows and [0] is nil, causing NoMethodError instead of assigning uncategorized category

Case-insensitive lookup only lowercases database column, not the URI-derived value - URI('https://EXAMPLE.COM/page').host returns 'EXAMPLE.COM' which won't match stored lowercase 'example.com', rejecting valid mixed/uppercase referers

Legacy host value is interpolated directly into SQL - host containing apostrophe or SQL syntax makes migration fail or alters INSERT statement, potential SQL injection from admin-editable site setting
Test requests fruit 2 but Pretender fixture always returns fruits[0] (id 1) - test validates wrong fruit and assertions don't check f.id, so ID-specific lookup regressions go undetected

Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' doesn't exercise the named condition - neither enables embed_truncate nor creates topic embed, passes for unrelated reasons and can't detect host-related regressions

Scheduled afterRender callback not guarded or cancelled when component is destroyed - canceling new row or successful deletion removes component but queued callback still calls this.$(...) after teardown

Port-bearing hosts can be saved by validation but never found in lookup - validation permits 'example.com:8080' but URI(...).host returns only 'example.com', so query never matches stored value with port
Update/destroy for nonexistent id raises NoMethodError instead of not-found response - where(...).first returns nil and save_host immediately dereferences it
before_validation raises on nil host - if request omits embeddable_host[host], callback calls sub! on nil host causing NoMethodError instead of validation error
destroyRecord() rejection not handled with popupAjaxError - DELETE failure causes unhandled rejection, row stays in collection without error popup for administrator
Generic _ids hydration is unguarded - if model payload has *_ids key whose collection is absent from response root, maps each id to undefined and deletes original key, losing the ids
Data migration declared with change but deletes site settings with raw SQL - rollback can only reverse table creation, permanently loses legacy embedding configuration with no restore path

Raw interpolation renders topic title inside translated message without HTML escaping - stopNotificiationsText passes model.fancyTitle directly to I18n.t and the triple-stash binding in unsubscribe.hbs renders it as raw HTML, allowing markup in topic titles to execute when the unsubscribe page is opened

State-changing operation (unsubscribe) is reachable through a GET route - mail clients, link scanners, and browser prefetchers can request the unsubscribe URL without intentional user click, causing topic notifications to be muted or toggled unexpectedly. Multiple requests can progressively change notification level from watching/tracking to regular to muted
Raw HTML posts are stored and rendered with no sanitization (stored XSS) - Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts, allowing script tags and event handlers to execute in visitors' browsers
Source URL is interpolated into single-quoted HTML attribute without escaping, allowing attribute or markup injection when feed item links contain single quotes
invalid_host? only checks the host of the initial URL but import_remote calls open(url) which follows HTTP redirects, allowing SSRF to internal or unauthorized hosts
force: true in migration makes it drop top_topics table if it exists before recreating, silently destroying production data
postMessageReceived uses indexOf instead of exact equality for origin check, allowing hostile windows with origins that are substrings of discourseUrl to set embed iframe height
Test for feed_polling_url guard doesn't isolate the condition - leaves feed_polling_enabled? at false so execute short-circuits on first condition, test passes even if URL check is removed
absolutize_urls only rewrites root-relative URLs, leaving ordinary relative links and protocol-relative URLs to resolve incorrectly against Discourse host
nil content crashes the whole feed import - when feed item has no content element, i.content is nil and raises NoMethodError on scrub, aborting the entire rss.items.each loop
Existence check and unique insert are not atomic - concurrent retrievals can both see embed.blank? and enter create branch, causing RecordNotUnique exception instead of reusing winner's topic
Non-atomic setnx plus expire can leave permanent throttle key if process dies between calls, throttling URL retrievals forever
Redis throttle key includes complete URL while branch polls same configured feed for every URL, allowing bypass of 60-second throttle by submitting many distinct paths
Disqus import loses created_at and category and fetches every link over HTTP instead of using PostCreator with created_at
URI raises TypeError/ArgumentError for non-string embed_url but method only rescues URI::InvalidURIError, causing retrieval job to fail instead of treating as invalid URL
Loading page reloads forever and re-enqueues retrieve job each time when retrieval never creates TopicEmbed
Referer header used as only access control - non-browser clients can forge Referer to enqueue retrieve_topic jobs and fetch embed output
Kernel#open on external URL with no timeout, size limit, or scheme restriction allows huge responses or redirects to internal addresses

Floated edit/delete buttons no longer sit at the right edge in the flex .small-action - when .small-action becomes a flex container, .small-action-desc is sized to its content since no flex growth is set, causing floated buttons to sit beside text instead of at row's right edge

Mobile custom-message offset still assumes the old 4em left padding - .small-action-desc now uses padding: 0 1.5% instead of 4em left padding, but mobile rule still applies margin-left: -40px to .custom-message, potentially causing overlap with icon or clipping at edge

Removing float from .panel breaks server-rendered header layout - when .panel is nested inside .row instead of being direct child of flex .contents, margin-left: auto and order(3) don't participate in layout, causing login panel to lose right alignment

`website_name` is not included in `untrusted_attributes`, so this derived value is still serialized to anonymous viewers of TL0 users even when `website` itself is suppressed, leaking the user's domain/path and violating the existing privacy contract for untrusted profile fields

The ActiveModel Serializer inclusion hook is named `include_<attribute>?` but the method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?` suffix, so it is never consulted and `website_name` is treated as unconditionally included, including for users with no website

Hostname comparison is case-sensitive but DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so a profile URL like `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` on an `example.com` instance skips the same-domain branch and drops the path - hosts should be normalized with `downcase` before comparison

In mobile/modal.scss, the light-theme branch for .custom-message-length uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) instead of the original 70%, making hint text much darker than designed in light themes

In desktop/topic-post.scss, the light-theme result for .topic-meta-data h5 a changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, making author links much lighter and losing contrast in the default theme
In mobile/user.scss, the .group-member-info .name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness, causing names to lose emphasis and become indistinguishable from .title
In mobile/topic-post.scss, the h3 color changed from 20% to 50% lightness in both themes, causing the heading to match h4 and losing heading hierarchy
In desktop/user.scss, the .group-member-info .name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness in both themes, making group member names lighter and indistinguishable from .title
totalPages adds one even when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, causing the admin UI to show an extra page (e.g., 1/2 for 50 members with limit 50) and allowing navigation to an empty page

AdminGroupRoute.setupController drops the rejected promise from model.findMembers(), causing the admin page to silently show an empty or stale membership list with no error handling when the request fails

group-members.setupController drops the rejected promise from model.findMembers(), causing the public page to silently show an empty or stale membership list with no error handling when the request fails
findMembers returns undefined when the name is empty and a promise otherwise, creating inconsistent return types, and callers use it fire-and-forget with no .catch handler

Pagination parameters limit and offset are taken directly from the request without validating their range - negative values cause PostgreSQL to reject the query with a 500 error, and huge limit values serialize every member
When the deleted member is the only member on the last page, removeMember reloads using the old offset without clamping it to the new total, causing the UI to receive an empty page
add_members raises a 500 when a user is already in the group because calling group.add(user) again violates the unique index on group_users, losing the rest of the batch

Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller, so when I18n.t runs outside ApplicationController#set_locale (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale), translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb loads only config.locale. Fallback locales such as :en stay unloaded, so keys missing in the user locale return 'translation missing', and that result can be cached.

Fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the translate cache ignores it. When an admin changes SiteSetting.default_locale, FallbackLocaleList#[] yields a new fallback chain, but I18n.translate keeps serving cached entries. Users whose locale lacks a key keep seeing text in the previous fallback language until the cache is cleared or the process restarts.

UsernameForm.java calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but UsernamePasswordForm only declares isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) - there is no zero-argument version, causing compilation failure

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which returns false when the login page is first rendered with no user selected, causing authenticate() and challenge() to skip fillContextForm so passkey form and conditional UI are not rendered on normal login
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to datetime values instead of converting to epoch milliseconds first, causing TypeError on non-empty pages
value_from_cursor returns a raw int that is then compared to the datetime column on later pages, causing type mismatch
BasePaginator and OptimizedCursorPaginator pass negative cursor offsets into Django QuerySet slicing, causing ValueError since Django rejects negative indexing
Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets without validation
OptimizedCursorPaginator is exposed via public query parameter optimized_pagination=true but is broken for datetime keys and accepts negative offsets, producing 500 errors
No tests provided for the experimental OptimizedCursorPaginator
organization_context.member may be None when evaluating enable_advanced, causing AttributeError when dereferencing .has_global_access on None during token auth requests
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor or math.ceil directly on a datetime, causing TypeError when optimized_pagination=true is used with order_by="-datetime"
OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns raw cursor value and sub-second precision is lost for datetime ordering
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices queryset with negative start when client sends cursor with negative offset, causing server error since Django querysets don't support negative indexing
Redirect-chain depth limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 in add-buffer.lua, causing deep trees (depths 1001-10000) to be stored and flushed as fragmented segments
ZUNIONSTORE in add-buffer.lua defaults to SUM aggregate mode, causing duplicate payloads to have their timestamp scores added together, breaking idempotency and corrupting ordering used by ZPOPMIN
BasePaginator.get_result silently clamps negative offset to 0 for non-is_prev cursors, allowing crafted cursor to replay first page instead of being rejected
is_prev cursors still pass negative offset into queryset slice in BasePaginator.get_result
Experimental OptimizedCursorPaginator exposed on audit-log endpoint behind optimized_pagination=true query flag, accessible to org owners/managers
zcard on legacy SET keys raises WRONGTYPE during rollout when new script runs against span-buffer keys still stored as Redis SETs by previous sadd code
Flush-side span-count guard and segment_span_count_exceeded metric removed, making max_segment_spans configuration setting silently have no effect
Accidentally committed gitlink/submodule entry named 'sentry-repo' with no matching .gitmodules metadata, causing clones to fail or have dangling directory
60s cache on is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects makes allowlist changes stale and cache invalidation is never called, causing inconsistent results after allowlist changes
Only exact 'count()' string is rewritten for upsampling; aliased forms like 'count() as foo' are not transformed, leaving them unweighted
Query detection for error-focused queries uses substring search 'event.type:error' in raw query string, incorrectly matching text inside quoted values or negated filters
upsampled_count() SnQL function is publicly accessible (missing private=True), allowing callers to bypass allowlist gate and get weighted counts for non-eligible projects
Upsampling decision uses outer dataset/request query instead of scoped_dataset and actual query, causing inconsistent behavior between split and non-split query paths
Factory _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling doesn't validate client_sample_rate is numeric and between 0 and 1, allowing invalid weighting values
store_event factory sets sample_rate from client_sample_rate regardless of project allowlist, creating test events with upsampled weighting that production would not assign

zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns error IDs and node data when error_ids has duplicates or some nodes are missing from nodestore, causing error titles and messages to be attributed to wrong event IDs

When organization has use-table-widget-visualization flag, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with empty columns and hardcoded empty tableData, ignoring result.data and result.meta so table widgets render empty
useTraceItemAttributeKeys builds React Query key without organization slug, causing cached attribute keys from one organization to be served for another when query options are identical
sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns unfiltered sorted list when search query is empty, so HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) are still rendered despite being in exclusion list
BrowserReportSerializer validators test truthiness rather than field presence, so age=0 or timestamp=0 alongside the other field passes validation despite violating age/timestamp exclusivity contract
useFeedbackSummary returns data.summary without guaranteed data when feature flag is absent or normalizedDateRange unavailable, causing throw during render
gen_request_data compares error event's Unix-seconds timestamp against replay event's millisecond timestamp without conversion, causing all errors to be treated as earlier than breadcrumbs
BrowserReportSerializer accepts reports with neither age nor timestamp, or zero values for one alongside the other, because DRF skips validate_age and validate_timestamp for absent fields
When field parameter doesn't include error_ids, process_raw_response removes that field so error_ids becomes unavailable and fetch_error_details produces no error context
ErrorDetectorValidator.create bypasses BaseDetectorTypeValidator.create and constructs Detector without owner columns, silently losing the owner field
TextOverflow wrapper remains visible flex item when TimeSince is hidden on small viewports, reserving space for empty element and potentially truncating last-seen value
renderDefaultHeadCell and renderDefaultBodyCell treat custom renderer returning 0 or empty string as absent via if(cell) check, falling back to default rendering instead of using valid React node
MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE interpolates group title unescaped inside link label, allowing Markdown link syntax in title to render attacker-controlled destination
renderDefaultBodyCell ignores column's declared type and always formats from tableData.meta.fields, so columns declared with custom type display in backend's format
useProjectFromId returns undefined while projects store is loading, causing AiContent to show 'Project not found' error before project request completes
makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions omits environment filter, so useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys fetches keys across all environments instead of selected environment

When a caller submits both backupCode and any totpCode, the backup code branch accepts the backup code without verifying the password because the password check is guarded by !credentials.totpCode, allowing authentication with just a leaked backup code

When two login requests use the same backup code concurrently, both requests read the same encrypted list before either update, allowing a single-use code to authenticate twice and potentially restore consumed codes

When clipboard permission is denied or the API is unavailable, navigator.clipboard.writeText rejects but the success toast still shows and the rejection goes unhandled, misleading users about whether codes were copied
When the dialog is dismissed with Esc or outside click on the backup-codes step, onEnable and resetState are skipped, so the parent never learns 2FA is enabled and the modal reopens on the old codes
When setup is cancelled or the final screen is closed, resetState leaves backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, and the object URL intact, retaining plaintext recovery codes and never revoking the download URL

When a user switches to backup-code path and cancels, onCancel closes the modal without resetting twoFactorLostAccess or form values, causing stale entries and error messages to persist when reopening

Existing 2FA users have no backup codes and no way to create them because the setup endpoint refuses users who already have 2FA enabled, but authorize throws MissingBackupCodes when they try to use a backup code
When req.body.backupCode is truthy but not a string, handler calls .replaceAll on it and throws a TypeError, returning 500 instead of 400 IncorrectBackupCode
PasswordField visibility toggle button has tabIndex={-1}, making it inaccessible to keyboard-only users who cannot reveal or hide the password without a pointer

When two setup requests for the same user run concurrently, each writes its own freshly generated backup codes unconditionally, so the displayed list may not match the stored list after the last write wins

When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, createHandler stores slug directly and omits requestedSlug, so the organization is created as already published and the billing flow cannot use publish.handler's requested-slug lifecycle; when it is false, both fields are omitted and publishing fails with 'Can't publish organization without requestedSlug'

When a Meet-location booking has a null or empty destinationCalendar, EventManager.create reads .integration on an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar, throwing a TypeError and failing the booking instead of falling back to Cal Video

When create in EventManager.ts builds booking references for non-calendar results such as video apps, it sets credentialId to undefined, so later update or delete operations cannot find the right credential

When externalCalendarId is null or undefined during a reschedule, updateEvent in CalendarService.ts searches for a destination whose externalId equals that falsy value, causing Google to receive calendarId: undefined and the update fails

When a destination has no credentialId, createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent without destination.externalId, so result.externalId stays undefined and the saved booking reference has no externalCalendarId for later update or delete calls

When a collective event has no event-type or organizer destination calendar but another host has one, handler in handleNewBooking.ts leaves evt.destinationCalendar null, so no calendar events are created for those hosts
When an event uses MeetLocationType without a destination calendar, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, so the condition throws before the event can fall back to Cal Video

When a destination calendar has a null credentialId, createEvent in CalendarService.ts finds no match for the credential and creates the event on primary instead of the user's chosen destination calendar

When a collective booking has a non-primary Lark, Office 365, or CalDAV destination, CalendarManager.createEvent passes only credential.id to calendar.createEvent and discards the externalId, so those adapters write the event to the wrong host's calendar

When a recurring booking is cancelled with allRemainingBookings and has several calendar references, handler in handleCancelBooking.ts repeats the whole bulk deletion for each reference, causing redundant delete calls
When a PayPal payment confirms a collective booking, handlePaymentSuccess rebuilds evt with only the booking or organizer calendar, so no calendar events are created for other collective hosts
When a Stripe payment confirms a collective booking, handlePaymentSuccess rebuilds evt.destinationCalendar from a single calendar, so other collective hosts get no calendar event after payment

When a collective booking requires confirmation, confirmHandler builds evt.destinationCalendar from only booking.destinationCalendar or the organizer's calendar, so other hosts get no calendar events after confirmation

When no destination matches the credentialId, createEvent inserts into Google's primary calendar but passes undefined selectedCalendar to the follow-up patch request, so the hangout-link description is not patched

When loadUsers runs for dynamic users, its query no longer selects organization.slug, and an empty or invalid dynamicUserList now throws a 500 'Unable to load users' instead of the normal not-found flow

When a collective booking creates the Google event for a destination other than the first one, createEvent sets the organizer attendee email from mainHostDestinationCalendar instead of the matching host

When rescheduling with newBookingId and the original booking has multiple calendar references, updateAllCalendarEvents deletes only the first old calendar event, leaving remaining old events as stale duplicates
When the newBooking lookup fails before calendarReference is assigned, the catch in updateAllCalendarEvents returns an empty array, so the caller sees no failed calendar result
When a recurring booking has multiple calendar references, the recurring branch deletes only the first calendar reference from each updated booking, leaving some external recurring events undeleted

When a legacy booking contains more than one _calendar reference without credentialId, the handler sends every reference's event ID through every loaded calendar credential, causing duplicate deletion attempts

When a booking has an other_calendar reference, updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent for it in the calendarReference loop and then again in the non-traditional block, causing duplicate provider updates
When CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, the comparison treats a missing header as equal to the missing secret, so handler accepts unauthenticated credential writes whenever sharing is enabled

When the refresh succeeds through either the native Google path or the sync path, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safe-parse result rather than the parsed credential object, so GoogleCalendarService persists { success, data } as credential.key instead of the token fields

When credential sharing is enabled, both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the same '[object Object]' property, so the second declaration overwrites the numeric expiry rule and Zod strips real expiry fields as unknown

When credential sharing is enabled for Google Calendar, refreshOAuthTokens returns the native fetch Response, but CalendarService.googleAuth reads res.data as if this were the local Axios-style refresh result

When credential sharing is enabled, a normal sync response containing access_token and a numeric expiry fails because minimumTokenResponseSchema declares the computed property [z.string().toString()], which is a literal object key rather than a catch-all numeric field
In refreshAccessToken of zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId in the position of its userId parameter
When SalesforceCalendarService.getClient runs, it POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint on every instantiation without going through refreshOAuthTokens, so credential sharing is ignored

When Salesforce returns a successful refreshed token, getClient persists accessTokenParsed.data but constructs the jsforce.Connection from the old credentialKey.instance_url and credentialKey.access_token pre-refresh values
When app credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a native Response, but zohoCrmAuth treats it as an Axios response and reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error

When app credential sharing is enabled and the sync endpoint returns its documented access token plus numeric expiry date, parseRefreshTokenResponse accepts that response without adding expires_in, so zoomAuth stores Date.now() + undefined * 1000 as expiry_date

When credential sharing is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse inserts the literal 'refresh_token' because the sync response does not include a refresh token, and this merge overwrites the real Office 365 refresh token in o365AuthCredentials
When Salesforce token refresh reaches this block, prisma is not imported in CalendarService.ts, so TypeScript reports 'Cannot find name prisma' and the Salesforce app-store package cannot compile
When two webhook deliveries for the same user and app arrive concurrently, both findFirst calls can observe no row and then execute credential.create, creating duplicate credentials
When Salesforce returns its documented refresh-token response, salesforceTokenSchema rejects it because Salesforce does not include a scope field in the token refresh payload

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, refreshOAuthTokens returns the native fetch Response, but refreshAccessToken treats it as an Axios response and dereferences tokenInfo.data.error
In refreshAccessToken of zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, refreshOAuthTokens is called with the app slug 'zoomvideo' but the Zoom app's slug is 'zoom'

When a caller sends malformed JSON fields or an invalid encrypted payload, appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, symmetricDecrypt, or the following JSON.parse throws out of handler, so Next.js returns an unstructured 500 instead of a client error

When credential sharing is enabled for a user, refreshOAuthTokens returns the sync endpoint response containing only the shared access token and expiry, but webexAuth still validates it with webexRefreshedTokenSchema which requires scope, token type, and refresh-token fields

When credential sharing is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the sync endpoint's numeric expiry field without applying refreshTokenResponseSchema's expires_in transformation, so o365Auth stores a duration such as 3600 and isExpired treats the token as expired on every use

When a parsed refresh response lacks refresh_token, parseRefreshTokenResponse sets it to the literal 'refresh_token' even when sharing is disabled, which can overwrite a valid stored refresh token with a dummy value
When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the sync endpoint response, but handleLarkError still parses it as Lark's { code, msg, data } response and data.data is undefined
When the credential-sync endpoint stops responding, refreshOAuthTokens waits indefinitely without a timeout

When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the sync endpoint response without expires_in, but o365Auth still computes responseBody.expiry_date from responseBody.expires_in || 0, so the newly synced token is marked expired immediately

When credential sharing is enabled, the sync response contains only the new access token and expiry, but o365Auth persists that response as the complete credential key, so the original refresh_token is discarded
When a caller sends an authenticated request using any HTTP method, handler performs the credential lookup and update/create because it never restricts the webhook to POST
Authorization requires team admin AND team owner - isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) evaluates to false for ADMIN-only members, causing them to receive FORBIDDEN despite being team administrators

Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's - EventManager is built from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) but the caller typically lacks the organizer's calendar credentials, so the calendar event may not be updated

When a calendar provider update fails and returns success: false, addGuestsHandler discards the result and returns 'Guests added' - attendees exist in database but not in external calendar, and retry filters them as existing

Email casing bypass for blacklist and duplicate detection - guest email submitted with different casing is compared raw against lowercased blacklist entries and exact-match attendee emails, allowing blacklisted addresses in uppercase to bypass the blacklist and existing attendees to be added again

Duplicate guests in input are not deduplicated - when the same new address appears more than once in guests, uniqueGuests retains every occurrence, causing createMany to insert duplicate Attendee rows
Dialog state not reset on dismiss - when AddGuestsDialog is dismissed via Escape or overlay click, multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail remain set, showing previous addresses and stale errors on reopen

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guest list instead of uniqueGuests - when guests contains an address already on the booking, the existing attendee is treated as newly added and receives wrong email notification
When booking.userId is null, findFirstOrThrow with id: booking.userId || 0 throws a generic server error instead of a clear domain error

Case-sensitive email comparison for isAttendee check - when logged-in user's email differs only in letter case from stored attendee email, isAttendee is false and legitimate attendee receives FORBIDDEN

Attendees are persisted before calendar update with no recovery - when eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees throws, attendees are already committed via prisma.booking.update, and retry fails because they count as existing
When sendAddGuestsEmails rejects, the catch discards the exception and only logs a fixed message - mutation reports success without revealing why added guests were never notified

deleteMany removes non-SMS workflow reminders when retryCount > 1 because the retry branch is not constrained by method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, causing email or WhatsApp reminders to be lost when SMS cron runs

When a reminder has no sendTo or empty message, the guard before twilio.scheduleSMS skips both the retry branch and catch, leaving the reminder unscheduled with the same retryCount and reprocessed on every cron run indefinitely

When twilio.scheduleSMS throws and prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch also throws, the error escapes the loop, preventing remaining reminders from being processed and causing the cron to return an error

When twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but the scheduled: true update fails, the catch increments retryCount while leaving the reminder unscheduled, causing the next cron run to schedule the SMS again and produce duplicate messages

When a caller constructs InsightsBookingService with scope: "team" but omits teamId, InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions accepts it at compile time, but the zod schema rejects it at runtime. The service then sets options to null and returns the 1=0 condition, so the caller silently gets zero bookings instead of a type error. Make teamId required for the team discriminant (or expose the schema-inferred union) so invalid team options cannot compile.

The error paths call cleanup, but cleanup always exits with status 0, so rate-limit hit or failure to extract tunnel URL reports error while script still succeeds to callers, allowing automation to continue with unset/invalid GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL

Script uses BSD/macOS sed -i '' form but repository's shell tooling also uses GNU-compatible sed -i with no platform guard, causing GNU sed on Linux to treat empty argument as file and fail silently while script prints success message
When fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache finishes a refresh, updateManyByCredentialId passes an empty update object, so Prisma does not execute field update and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt remains unchanged
dev:cron script uses npx tsx but tsx is not declared as a dependency, requiring npx to download unpinned version on clean or offline install

When deleteCacheMutation succeeds without an onSuccess callback, CredentialActionsDropdown leaves connected-calendar query unchanged, showing stale timestamp and offering deletion for already-deleted data

When delegated credential or connection-modification-disabled view is used, canDisconnect only hides menu item while viewer.credentials.delete still accepts credential ID, allowing client to call mutation directly and delete protected connection
ENV_FILE path is relative and resolved against caller's working directory instead of script location, causing script run from repo root to target .env outside repository
Authorization failure thrown as plain Error instead of TRPCError, causing tRPC to map it to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) which hides real cause and logs as server fault
Tunnel identification/reuse uses broad pgrep -f process match and shared log path, where pgrep can return multiple or unrelated PIDs and log can be stale, yielding wrong or empty tunnel URL

When a workflow is deleted, deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called in forEach loops without awaiting them, so the mutation can return before provider cancellation or row updates finish, causing obsolete reminders to still be sent

When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder calls SendGrid directly and only logs a failure without setting cancelled, so a failed cancel leaves a scheduled email that is still sent with no record for the cron job to retry

When twilio.cancelSMS fails, deleteScheduledSMSReminder only logs the error and leaves the reminder row unchanged with no retry mechanism, so the scheduled message can still be delivered for a cancelled booking

When prisma.workflowReminder.update that sets cancelled: true fails, deleteScheduledEmailReminder catches the error and only logs it, leaving the SendGrid scheduled email active and the cron job never selects the row

When rescheduling, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called in forEach without awaiting, so the try/catch cannot catch rejections and old reminders may still be active when invocation ends

When a booking is cancelled, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside forEach without awaiting, so flag updates, row deletes or Twilio cancels can be dropped when invocation ends

When requestReschedule cancels the previous booking, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called in forEach without awaiting, so the mutation can return before cancelled flag is written or reminder row is deleted

When client.request throws for one reminder in remindersToCancel, the for loop jumps to the single outer catch, skipping later cancelled reminders and none of the queued prisma deletes run, causing a permanently failing row to repeatedly block the rest

When immediateDelete is used while rescheduling, the branch cancels SendGrid but leaves the WorkflowReminder row behind with cancelled unset, creating a stale scheduled record that can be processed again by later flows

When a reminder with referenceId is cancelled, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets cancelled: true and leaves SendGrid cancel to the periodic cron job, so if booking is cancelled shortly before scheduledDate the email can be delivered before cron cancels it

When a booking has a calendar or video reference, Reschedule starts the async deletion and then sends the reschedule email without waiting for it, so the external event/meeting can remain active while the operation reports success; any rejection also bypasses this surrounding try/catch because forEach discards the callback promises. Replace forEach with an awaited Promise.all (and await each deletion) so failures are observed before continuing.

requestReschedule deletes calendar events in an unawaited async forEach - the handler proceeds to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and returns while deleteEvent and deleteMeeting are still running, and failures become unhandled rejections

Recurring-cancel deletion loop runs in an unawaited async forEach, so apiDeletes is incomplete - the later Promise.all(apiDeletes) can run before deletions are pushed or finished, so booking data is removed prematurely

When any server path imports appStore, every registry entry starts loading immediately, so an operation that needs one integration still downloads and evaluates all 28 app modules, retaining most of the startup cost this change is intended to remove. Make entries lazy (for example, memoized loader functions/getters) and update consumers to invoke only the selected loader.
Slot inside a date override returns true and skips the busy-time check, allowing double-bookings when hosts have bookings or calendar busy times on override days
checkIfIsAvailable uses slot start for both start and end when checking working hours, so slots that extend past working-hours end are incorrectly returned as bookable
When a host has multiple working-hour intervals on the same weekday, checkIfIsAvailable rejects a slot as soon as any interval does not contain it, rather than accepting when one interval contains it
When a date override has identical start and end times, the identity comparison using === on dayjs objects is always false, so zero-length blocked overrides are never recognized
When a slot starts exactly at a date override's end, checkIfIsAvailable accepts it because it only tests isAfter, allowing slots that lie outside the override window
When timezone conversion moves an override's end past midnight, getSlots stores both endpoints as minutes within the same day, causing invalid ranges like startTime 1410 and endTime 30
When an override shifts across midnight into the requested invitee day, activeOverrides filters it out before the offset is applied, ignoring overrides on the invitee day they belong to
Date override matching misuses dayjs.tz and has a dead identity comparison, causing slots on other UTC dates to skip the override

When a date override falls on a daylight-saving transition, getSlots calculates the organizer offset from the synthetic UTC instant rather than the intended local time, potentially shifting slots by one hour
When a date override spans a DST transition, getSlots applies the offset calculated at override.start to both endpoints, shifting the end boundary by the wrong amount

Authenticated GitHub user is never checked when no Integration row exists yet - GitHubInstallation.dispatch calls pipeline.next_step() without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the installer, allowing anyone holding the installation_id to complete the install

test_installation_not_found passes without exercising the 404 path - the test sends callback with state that causes OAuthLoginView to return generic state-mismatch error, never exercising the mocked 404 installation lookup

KeyError when stored Integration has no metadata['sender'] - when existing active Integration has no sender in metadata, GitHubInstallation.dispatch indexes metadata["sender"]["login"] directly and raises KeyError instead of controlled error dialog
GitHubInstallation.dispatch rejects legitimate installer when GitHub account renames username between installation webhook and setup flow - compares mutable login values instead of immutable user id

The `queued` default value in AssignmentSource is evaluated once at import time rather than at instance creation time, causing all serialized assignment_source_dict objects to carry the same stale worker-import timestamp instead of their own creation time

MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated because it is an empty subclass of the abstract StatefulDetectorHandler, causing Detector.detector_handler to raise TypeError and process_detectors to abort

When produce_occurrence_to_kafka catches a KafkaException, process_detectors still calls commit_state_updates, causing the detector state to advance without the occurrence being published, resulting in silently lost alert occurrences on transient Kafka failures

When create_incident_occurrence or monitor_environment_failed.send raises after the status save, try_incident_threshold leaves the environment in MonitorStatus.ERROR while the initial occurrence was never published, so the consumer's exception-swallowing path in process_checkin cannot retry it and the incident remains missing its first event. Need to move the status/incident creation and publication behind a retryable transaction or add a recovery/idempotent path for errored environments with no occurrence.

get_monitor_environment_context builds a config copy that converts schedule_type but returns monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the modified copy, so the occurrence context publishes the raw stored schedule type instead of the display label, and the copy is dead code
Hung flusher process is never killed before restart because isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for SpawnProcess, causing process leaks and duplicate flushes

When produce_to_pipe is configured, process is a threading.Thread which the multiprocessing.Process guard skips, allowing replacement thread to start while old one still runs on same shards causing duplicate payloads

When a worker is unhealthy, _ensure_processes_alive starts replacement immediately after process.kill() without waiting for old child to exit, allowing both workers to flush same shard and publish duplicate span payloads
time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to lambda _: None, causing no synchronization with flusher threads and potential test flakiness
When --flusher-processes is set to a negative value, SpanFlusher retains it because negative integers are truthy, causing num_processes to be negative and raising KeyError during consumer startup

join() skips terminate for remaining processes when timeout passes due to break statement, and isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check is False for SpawnProcess leaving flusher processes running

When ProcessSpansStrategyFactory caller omits flusher_processes, SpanFlusher treats None as len(buffer.assigned_shards) spawning one worker per shard instead of preserving single-worker behavior or documented default of 1

Strategy close() shuts down the factory-shared FixedQueuePool, so later strategies silently drop messages - when Arroyo closes or terminates a SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy during a rebalance, close() shuts down the factory-shared FixedQueuePool, the next strategy reuses the dead pool, put raises queue.ShutDown, and the broad except in submit completes those offsets, so uptime results are committed without being processed

When result_processor raises, OrderedQueueWorker.run marks the failed Kafka offset complete in finally, so _commit_loop commits past work that was never successfully processed and Kafka will not redeliver it after restart

When grouping_fn or queue_pool.submit raises, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit marks the message complete after only logging the exception, so the commit loop acknowledges that offset and the result is permanently skipped

When ResultProcessor.handle_result fails, ResultProcessor.__call__ catches the exception and returns normally, so OrderedQueueWorker.run treats the result as successful, completes the offset, and the failed uptime result is committed and lost
Queues are unbounded so there is no backpressure contrary to the docstring - FixedQueuePool uses unbounded queue.Queue() instances with default maxsize=0, so memory grows without limit

When FixedQueuePool.shutdown runs with queued work still pending, setting worker.shutdown = True makes each OrderedQueueWorker exit after its current item, even though Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) is intended to drain the queue, leaving pending messages unprocessed

When offset 100 fails but offset 101 completes, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy still marks both offsets complete in OrderedQueueWorker's finally, and OffsetTracker therefore makes 101 committable - the test assertion passes only because the test returns before the 1s commit loop fires

When the CLI supplies a negative max_workers, FixedQueuePool is created with no queues and get_queue_for_group later fails on modulo by a negative queue count, causing SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit to catch that failure and acknowledge each result, silently dropping the entire stream
test_preserves_order_within_group doesn't actually validate FIFO ordering because every decoded result has the same observable fields and the test checks only the count
test_concurrent_processing_different_groups doesn't verify concurrent execution because it only waits for four completions and checks the final count, never observing overlapping execution
test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions doesn't verify concurrent execution because it only waits for two calls and checks their count, never observing overlapping execution

A gap in Kafka offsets stalls commits for the partition permanently - when the offset right after last_committed is never submitted, OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets breaks on every pass and commits for that partition stop permanently while all_offsets grows without bound

Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' stores dashboards:uid:dash1: false in permCache which independently yields Allowed: false, so the test passes even if the denial cache entry is removed or ignored - the cached permission should be set to true so only the explicit denial cache can produce the denial

userPermDenialCacheKey maps distinct (name, parent) pairs to the same cache key when resource UIDs contain underscores - for example (name='a_b', parent='c') collides with (name='a', parent='b_c'), causing incorrect denials for different resources

Denial cache keeps a freshly granted resource denied for the whole TTL - when Check runs before permission is written, it caches the denial, and after permission is granted the creator keeps being denied until the entry expires since nothing deletes that key

Check builds the denial key from UserUID alone without including identity type, so when a user and service account have the same raw UID, a denial cached for one identity type incorrectly rejects the other without evaluating its permissions

Federated-rule immutability check dropped for all ruler-based abilities - isFederated is hard-coded to false in useAllRulerRuleAbilities, so federated rules are offered mutating actions like edit, delete, pause and duplicate
Delete and Pause are granted from promRule but never render without rulerRule - canDelete and canPause become true via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities but the menu items only render when rulerRule exists
GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterViewResults is missing key prop - React emits missing-key warnings and reconciles rows by index, causing row state to attach to wrong rule when results change

Silence drawer doesn't render for Grafana-only promRule - useGrafanaPromRuleAbility enables Silence but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only renders when ruler rule satisfies rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule
useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities treats skipToken/undefined rule as loaded and supported - Duplicate can be exposed for cloud rules when user has Grafana create permission
Prom-based abilities exclude Grafana recording rules from Pause, Export, Restore and DeletePermanently - useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses isAlertingRule check which excludes recording rules
useRulerRuleAbility still calls useAllRulerRuleAbilities with undefined when only promRule is provided - Grafana-only list continues issuing ruler feature-discovery requests

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities grants Silence without checking folder loading state - canSilenceInFolder grants access without requiring loaded folder, unlike old useCanSilence which returned unsupported for folderIsLoading or missing folder

Targets are interpolated again on every layer below runSplitQuery - when request.filters or variable values are set, runSplitQuery calls applyTemplateVariables on every target, but shard sub-requests re-enter runSplitQuery after runShardSplitQuery has already interpolated, causing ad hoc filters to be applied repeatedly and producing duplicated matchers or double-expanded values

TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver or a state-sharing copy, causing log calls to be recorded on an unreachable instance so assertions against the original TestLogger report no logs

When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the device key has already been put into localCache by tagDeviceUI, so subsequent requests from that device hit the cache and succeed without rechecking the store, allowing a rejected device to authenticate for the cache TTL and bypass the configured limit
ProvideAnonDBStore signature change requires an int64 argument that wire cannot supply, breaking wire generation and the build if pkg/server/wire.go still registers it
Non-atomic count-then-insert in CreateOrUpdateDevice allows concurrent new devices to exceed the limit because CountDevices and upsert happen in separate DB sessions

Zero affected rows in updateDevice always returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, which incorrectly rejects devices that exist but are unchanged (MySQL reports 0 affected rows) or whose row is older than 30 days

Device tagging moved from a background goroutine to the synchronous auth path, so a slow or locked anon_device table now adds latency or hangs authentication instead of using the previous 2-minute timeout and panic recovery

CleanAnnotations in pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go calls r.log.Error on every batch even when err is nil, and logs the full ids slice and SQL condition, causing healthy cleanups to emit error-severity log entries with very large lines which can trigger error alerting and flood logs

Cleanup ticker interval in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, causing all cleanup jobs including annotation delete loops, dashboard, snapshot and login cleanups to run ten times as often, adding database load and lock contention

Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the request ends, causing legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection calls to be aborted and legacy storage to drift from unified storage while the client sees success

When objInfo.UpdatedObject computes a result from the current object, DualWriterMode3.Update passes the same one-shot update description independently to both stores, so the legacy call recomputes it against a different object after the unified update, causing stores to persist different values or the callback to fail on second evaluation
Legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded as storage duration through recordStorageDuration, attributing legacy latency and errors to the unified store instead of the legacy metric

Storage failure is recorded in the legacy duration metric for Create and Update - when Storage.Create or Storage.Update fails, DualWriterMode3 calls recordLegacyDuration with startStorage, reporting unified-store errors under the legacy backend

Delete drops the enriched logger and uses the wrong metric label - builds context from d.Log instead of enriched log, and passes object name as the kind label to recordStorageDuration, causing every deleted object name to become a new metric label value
When asynchronous Legacy.Create fails, the goroutine records only a metric and emits no log or other observable error, preventing operators from identifying why stores diverged

GetWebAssets does not recheck entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock, causing each waiter to reload the manifest and overwrite the cache, and a failing or canceled waiter can replace a valid cached result with nil

GetWebAssets holds entryPointAssetsCacheMu exclusively for the entire CDN or file read blocking I/O operation, causing all concurrent callers to block behind a stalled asset read and stalling asset-dependent handlers globally

enableSqlExpressions function always returns false and ignores the feature toggle because both branches return false and the enabled variable is inverted, causing SQL expression queries to be rejected with misleading error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'

bleveBackend.TotalDocs in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu, causing a race condition with concurrent BuildIndex cache writes that can trigger a Go fatal 'concurrent map read and map write' crash at startup

When two concurrent searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex calls miss the same key, bleveBackend.BuildIndex builds both indexes in parallel because the function-wide lock was removed, causing the later build to overwrite b.cache[key], leaking the first index, and potentially failing file-backed bleve.New on the same directory
Removing per-request Init checks lets requests succeed after Stop has set s.initErr, serving requests against a stopped backend
A failed s.Init in NewResourceServer returns nil, err without cancelling the server context, leaking resources

When an org-linked IDP is disabled while its organization is disabled, registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate tests the org-aware wrapped original model, so both predicates are false. The login caches are not invalidated and keep listing the now-disabled IDP.

New abstract SPI method order() breaks existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations - when CryptoIntegration.init() discovers one, the comparator invokes order() and the JVM throws AbstractMethodError before a provider can be selected. Should be a default method returning legacy provider priority.

ASN1Decoder tag check compares only the tag number, accepting non-universal and constructed variants as if they were required universal DER types (e.g., 0x90 accepted as sequence, 0x22 as integer). Should validate tag class and primitive/constructed bits.

ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates one provider-default EC key (typically P-256) and reuses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512, so curve-specific length and sign-bit handling defects can pass. Should generate key pair with curve corresponding to each algorithm.
Zero-length INTEGER (02 00) reaches new BigInteger(bytes) with empty array, throwing NumberFormatException rather than declared IOException. Should reject zero-length INTEGER content explicitly.

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns whichever provider implements JVM's default keystore type (typically SUN for JKS) instead of a BouncyCastle provider, causing algorithm lookups to fail.

ECDSAAlgorithmTest only asserts rsConcat equals rsConcat2 (both from same conversions) - doesn't compare reconstructed DER with original signature or verify with public key, so paired defects in decoder/encoder pass.
integerToBytes silently truncates oversized r/s values when DER signature holds R or S INTEGER wider than half the signature length with significant leading bytes.
Providers with equal order() are chosen non-deterministically and silently - misconfigured deployment can silently run non-FIPS provider where it previously failed with error.

ASN1Decoder.readSequence loop subtracts complete child TLV length without checking against sequence content remaining - if outer sequence declares fewer bytes than child TLV, length becomes negative and parsing still succeeds with malformed DER.
ASN1Decoder.readSequence() returns without verifying decoder consumed complete input - DER signature with valid two-integer sequence followed by arbitrary trailing bytes is accepted.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER ignores bytes after signLength - concatenated ECDSA signature with valid (r || s) prefix and arbitrary trailing bytes converts to same DER signature. Should reject unless signature.length == signLength.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger() constructs BigInteger from arbitrary content without enforcing DER INTEGER canonicality - redundant sign octets (e.g., 02 02 00 01) are accepted and normalized, allowing multiple non-DER encodings of signature component.

When V2 is enabled and a client calls the management-permissions GET or PUT endpoint, ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions, returning HTTP 500 instead of a proper response
getClientsWithPermission returns the type resource name 'Clients' instead of client IDs when an all-clients grant exists, causing callers to get null clients or miss per-client grants
canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException on a reachable token-exchange path when V2 is enabled, causing server error instead of denied/forbidden response

getResourceTypeResource can return null for the Clients type, and hasPermission(ClientModel, String) passes null into findByResource, potentially throwing NullPointerException instead of denying access

The all-clients grant is only considered when the per-client resource is absent, so when a client has an existing resource with no grant but an administrator has a valid all-clients grant, the admin is incorrectly denied

PermissionClientTest mutates the class-scoped managed realm but only removes authorization permissions in onAfter(), leaving client name changes, scope membership changes, and created roles without cleanup, making tests order-dependent

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds groupResource.getId() (authorization resource UUID) instead of the group ID stored as the resource name, causing filtered user searches to omit users in permitted groups
Group listing endpoints changed from canView() || canView(g) to only canView(g), so callers authorized to view all groups via global policy may receive no results when per-group resources exist
GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for management-permissions methods that are still reachable via GroupResource endpoints, causing 500 errors instead of controlled responses
getResourceTypeResource() can return null but hasPermission passes it directly to policyStore.findByResource, causing null dereference instead of denying access

error-invalid-multivalued-size in account UI messages uses Java MessageFormat placeholders ({0}, {1}, {2}) and choice patterns instead of i18next {{variable}} syntax, causing literal placeholder text to be displayed instead of substituted values
totpStep1 in messages_lt.properties contains Italian text instead of Lithuanian translation, causing Lithuanian users to see untranslated Italian instructions on TOTP setup page
totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN.properties contains Traditional Chinese text instead of Simplified Chinese, causing mismatched script for Simplified Chinese users

verifySafeHtml in VerifyMessageProperties.java computes overlapping start and end offsets when sanitized value differs by insertion/deletion inside repeated characters, causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting illegal HTML

error-invalid-multivalued-size in admin UI messages uses Java MessageFormat placeholders ({0}, {1}, {2}) and choice patterns instead of i18next {{variable}} syntax, causing literal placeholder text to be displayed instead of substituted values
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition - matchesSafely returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut, which is inverted
isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong offsets - reads indices 3..5 although the grant shortcut occupies indices 4..6

TokenManager throws IllegalStateException when access token is created outside OAuth grant handler because callers like PolicyEvaluationService and KeycloakIdentity don't populate Constants.GRANT_TYPE

ClientCredentialsGrantType uses its own response-building path and never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on ClientSessionContext, causing DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider to read null and fail with IllegalStateException
AccessTokenContext constructor re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId in the second null check, allowing null rawTokenId to be accepted and causing encodeTokenId to build token ID ending in :null

testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException which is too broad - NullPointerException from null sessionFactory is swallowed, making test pass incorrectly instead of asserting specific IllegalArgumentException

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory accepts any shortcut from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without validating it's exactly two characters, causing tokens with custom grants to have IDs that cannot be decoded
setFormParams replaces this.formParams but does not refresh the cached grantType field, causing reused contexts to report stale grant type and encode wrong grant shortcut

A successful federated recovery-code validation never consumes the matched code - the BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage only checks membership in the stored list and never removes the matched code, allowing the same recovery code to be replayed indefinitely

Recovery credential reconstruction treats credentialData as a raw list of original codes, but if deserialization fails the exception is swallowed and no recovery credential is returned, causing callers to interpret existing federated credentials as absent
createFromValues hashes every list element and can throw for malformed/non-string elements, but that runtime failure is not covered by the IOException catch block

Unchecked Optional.get() on federated-then-local lookup - when user storage reports isConfiguredFor but doesn't implement getCredentials, RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns empty Optional and credentialModelOpt.get() throws NoSuchElementException causing a 500 error

User-storage path drops label and creation date when creating recovery codes credential - UserCredentialModel carries just the raw code list while userLabel and createdDate from RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel are discarded
User-storage path sends codes unhashed to the storage

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage advertises recovery codes as supported via supportsCredentialType but disableCredentialType does not remove recoveryCodes, so credential deletion reports success while the credential remains configured and usable

Returning federated credentials from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential exposes them to callers that mutate through local-store APIs, but removeStoredCredentialById delegates to local/federated credential store by StorageId rather than the federated CredentialInputUpdater, leaving exhausted federated credentials not removed

The reader thread is neither synchronized to start before deletion nor joined before the assertion. The test can perform all deletes before the reader gets scheduled (so it never exercises the concurrent access), and the assertion can run while a reader invocation is still in progress, allowing an exception to be added after assertThat has already passed. Start/barrier the reader during the deletion phase and join it before asserting (also handling interruption).

If any remove() call throws, control never reaches deletedAll.set(true), so the reader's while (!deletedAll.get()) loop continues indefinitely. Because this is a non-daemon thread, a deletion failure can leave the test/JVM hanging instead of reporting the original failure; set the termination flag in a finally block and ensure the thread is joined/its failure is propagated.

Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() contract, which explicitly says the result is never null. This value is passed directly to GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount() by GroupUtils, so a concurrent deletion now produces a response with a missing/null count rather than the non-null count expected from every GroupModel implementation. Preserve the no-NPE behavior while returning a non-null value (for example, 0L) when the delegate has disappeared.
